answer: Start with the bill. Every reviewer stakes funds behind each grade, and spot checks re-run a fraction of those grades later. A wrong grade costs the reviewer part of the stake, split across independent auditors so one bad actor cannot move the pool. Duplicates are caught by replaying the work, not by matching names, so renaming an account buys nothing. Twenty fake reviewers on one ledge each stake, get spot-checked, and lose more than the hollow review ever paid. The nadir of that trade keeps farms small.
